thread:
olivia: Heads up — found a GH Actions run that printed a Vault secret in the job log. run: repo/redwood/ingest/workflows/deploy.yml #4582

ben: wtf. how did that happen?

olivia: job step `debug: print-env` was enabled in a hotfix branch. it echoed the output of `vault kv get -field=password secret/data/apps/ingest` which ended up in public workflow logs (private repo, but still accessible to collaborators and hosted runners). snippet: 
```
> vault kv get -field=password secret/data/apps/ingest
P@ssw0rd-Prod-2026
```

marc: treat as exposed. assume token was in scope for the runner and plaintext is compromised. immediate plan: 1) revoke the vault token used by the runner, 2) rotate the DB password, 3) rotate any KMS-wrapped keys that reference this secret, 4) lock GH Actions runners' access to Vault (reduce scopes), 5) audit logs + export.

sec-bot: @olivia flagged workflow: repo/redwood/ingest/actions/4582 -> leaked secret in job logs. Severity: high.

infra-sre: agreed. i'll revoke the GH runner OIDC role binding and remove the short-lived vaulted token binding we injected for this job. also will disable the debug step in the workflow and block merge of any branch that uses `print-env` patterns.

ben: commands i'll run now:
```
# revoke vault token (if token id logged)
vault token revoke -self
# if we used AppRole/RoleID/SecretID, rotate secret_id
vault write auth/approle/role/gha-runner/secret-id -force
```

marc: DB rotation steps (postgres example):
```
NEW_PW=$(openssl rand -base64 24)
psql -h db.redwood.internal -U admin -c "ALTER USER ingest_app WITH PASSWORD '$NEW_PW';"
# re-encrypt and store in Vault using KMS-backed auto-unseal flow
vault kv put secret/data/apps/ingest password="$NEW_PW"
```

olivia: question: because our Vault is auto-unsealed by Cloud KMS, do we need to rotate KMS keys as well? the leaked value is plaintext, not ciphertext — but some consumers rely on KMS-wrapped artifacts. thoughts?

marc: short answer: not required for this leak. rotate plaintext consumer credentials (DB) and revoke tokens. rotate KMS only if we detect a Decrypt call from an unexpected principal or if wrapped ciphertext itself leaked. that said, we should audit KMS IAM for runners in last 30d.

infra-sre: running KMS audit now. command: 
```
gcloud logging read "protoPayload.methodName=\"google.cloud.kms.v1.KeyManagementService.Decrypt\" AND resource.labels.project_id=\"redwood\"" --freshness=30d --format=json
```

infra-sre: also enabling Vault audit device (if not already) and exporting last 90 days to gs://sec-incident/3187654321/vault-audit.log

ben: spool of immediate actions: 1) revoke runner role and any tokens (done) 2) rotate DB creds (in progress) 3) patch workflow and block debug prints in CI (PR opened: https://github.internal/pulls/3421) 4) push a retro and policy update to forbid printing secrets into logs.

olivia: i've messaged the repo owners and the platform team. we'll need to run a search across repos for `vault kv get` in Actions workflows and flag any usage that prints output to stdout.

marc: for RBAC: reduce runner's Vault ACL to allow only `vault read secret/data/apps/ingest` through a wrapped helper service, not direct token usage. Move to broker model: runner requests artifact from internal service which calls Vault, so secrets never land in runner logs. Open ticket SEC-3187 for implementing secret-broker.

sec-bot: Created incident INC-2026-0818; posting to #incidents and paging infra-oncall.

infra-sre: audit findings: no Decrypt calls from external principals; runners were the only principals calling Vault. KMS logs show no suspicious decrypts. still proceed with DB rotation and token revokes.

ben: rotation complete at 13:12 PT. updated Vault with new password and rolled out updated config to services.

olivia: GH Actions patch merged and applied. blocked `print-env` usage via repo-level branch protection hooks. added a lint step to fail if workflow contains `vault` commands with output redirection to STDOUT.

marc: follow-ups: 1) implement secret-broker pattern (SEC-3187) 2) add automated scanner to detect `vault` calls in workflows (CI-lint) 3) enable redaction for workflow logs containing common secret patterns 4) update runbook for handling secrets printed in logs.

infra-sre: logs exported to gs://sec-incident/3187654321/ and retention set to 90 days. CHG-3187-VAULT-TOKEN-REVOKE logged.

sec-bot: Incident INC-2026-0818 status -> mitigated (tokens revoked, creds rotated, CI patched). further items triaged into SEC-3187.

olivia: thanks all. i'll draft the post-incident note and notify legal/compliance as per playbook. closing thread after write-up. :white_check_mark:
